United States President Donald Trump listens as Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr speaks at a campaign rally at Alico Arena on the campus of Florida Gulf Coast University, on Friday, October 23, 2026, in Fort Myers, Florida, the US [File: Mark Schiefelbein/AP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
United States Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has sparked uproar with comments he has made denying Arab contributions to mathematics, science and literature.
In a high-voltage rant on Monday, the US health secretary said, “There’s five hundred million Arabs in the world. And yet they don’t produce science. They don’t win the Nobel Prize. They don’t win the Fields Prize. They don’t win the Wolf Prize. They don’t produce literature.”
RFK Jr, who has been involved in anti-vaccine campaigns and has promoted a debunked theory linking vaccines to autism, made the comments during a US election campaign event in Grand Rapids, Michigan while supporting Republican nominee Mike Rogers, who is up against Arab-American Democrat nominee Abdul El-Sayed, in a tightly contested battle for Michigan’s Senate seat in next week’s midterm elections.
Critics said the comments were racist, Islamophobic and factually inaccurate, pointing to modern and historic Arab innovation in multiple fields.
Here’s how Arabs have made vital contributions to the human understanding of maths, science and literature through the centuries.
Arab contributions to maths, science and humanities
The period known as the Islamic Golden Age, from around 750 AD to 1258 AD, produced many key Arab contributions to medicine at a time when Europe was said to be in its Dark Ages. During this time, Arabic was the language of science and scholarship. ...

Binance shared donation records with Russian investigators, according to documents seen by Reuters [File: Dado Ruvic/Illustration/Reuters]By Heba Habib and ReutersPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
A Russian military court has sentenced an IT specialist to 13 years in prison for financing “terrorism” after the cryptocurrency exchange Binance gave Russian investigators details of his donations to Ukrainian fundraising campaigns.
The 2nd Western District Military Court on Monday convicted 49-year-old Yuri Belenkiy and sentenced him to three years in prison followed by 10 years in a strict-regime penal colony, according to a court statement.

Russian state news agency TASS reported that Belenkiy is a former IT director of the company DiHouse and that prosecutors had asked for 14 years. He was also fined 500,000 roubles ($6,300).
Belenkiy, who holds a Bulgarian residence permit, was detained in September last year when he flew to Moscow for a visit. He denied the charges, and his defence will appeal the verdict, according to TASS.
According to the RIA Novosti news agency, the court found that between August 2022 and March 2024, Belenkiy made 15 cryptocurrency transfers worth more than 120,000 roubles ($1,500) to fund Ukraine’s armed forces and the Azov battalion, which Russia designates a “terrorist” organisation. England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane kisses the Ballon d'Or trophy after receiving the award for the best male footballer at the London Palladium [Franck Fife/AFP]By Manasi PathakPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
Gently planting a kiss on the Ballon d’Or trophy, Harry Kane proudly lifted the shiny silverware into the air with a look of disbelief on his face.
The cameras flashed, the “home” crowd erupted in thunderous applause, and an unassuming winner basked in his moment of glory.

Hundreds of England fans had lined up outside the London Palladium for this moment, while millions more across the country had waited for it with bated breath. It was a day 25 years in the making.
For Kane, it was an achievement beyond belief and a victory too bold to dream of.
Monday’s hometown glory was Kane’s crowning moment – a testament to his remarkable talent and sheer consistency.
He was never the superstar – far from it. For years, he struggled for game time. Loaned from one club to another. Not a teenage prodigy. Not one to watch out for.
But that never deterred the boy from Leytonstone, who, year after year, put in the hard work and silenced the outside noise. Now, at 33 years old, when many of his peers are past their prime, Kane is peaking at the perfect time.
Often mocked for not winning trophies, Kane – it seemed – was busy making space for the ultimate prize: the Ballon d’Or – football’s most prestigious individual honour.

US President Donald Trump speaks to members of the media as he departs for the state of Texas at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, the United States, October 27, 2026 [Kevin Lamarque/Reuters]By Umar FarooqPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
United States President Donald Trump said he would respect the results of next week’s midterm elections if they were “honest,” as his administration expanded a legal battle to assert power over state authorities running the highly-watched contest on November 3.
“I will if they’re honest elections,” Trump responded to reporters on Tuesday when asked if he will respect the outcome even if his Republican Party loses control of the US Congress.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3US Justice Department to send election observers to California, New Jerseylist 2 of 3US Attorney General Todd Blanche defends Alaska Senate election lawsuitlist 3 of 3Trump administration sues California over noncitizens on voter rollsend of list
Trump’s remarks came a day after his Department of Justice (DOJ) threatened the northwestern state of Washington with legal action if it did not remove around 400 people it claims are not US citizens from its voter registration rolls.
“The timing of this request—one week before the General Election—is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results,” Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs said in a statement on Monday, addressing the request received in a letter that gave the state until Wednesday at noon local time to respond, or face what the DOJ called “emergency relief”.

An Arab-Israeli woman casts her ballot during Israel's general elections on October 27, 2026 in Umm al-Fahm, Israel [Amir Levy/Getty Images]By Daniel Khalili-TariPublished On 27 Oct 202627 Oct 2026
Prominent politicians from Arab-led lists have accused Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of inciting hatred against Palestinian citizens in the country, in an attempt to boost his electoral prospects.
Yousef Jabareen, leader of the Joint List, said in a video statement shared on social media on Tuesday that Netanyahu knew that “we can put an end to his bloody reign”. Meanwhile, Mansour Abbas, leader of the United Arab List, denounced Netanyahu’s comments as a “scare tactic to mobilise right-wing voters and drive them to the polls”.

In a series of posts on X on Tuesday, Netanyahu attacked Arab voters, describing them as “Muslim Brotherhood supporters” and accusing them of “raiding the polling stations and stealing the elections”.
In a separate post, Netanyahu referred to a picture of a large queue that appeared to show Palestinian citizens in Israel at a polling station, and called on right-wing Israelis to “go out and vote for Likud”, referring to his political party and describing the situation as a “matter of life and death for us”.
